QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_24

question.text: Lotus Private Equity Fund (Cat II) called INR 500 crore from LPs over its investment period. At final exit, total distributions to LPs are INR 900 crore, and residual NAV is INR 200 crore. What is the fund's TVPI (Total Value to Paid-in) multiple?

explanation.text: The Logic: TVPI = (Distributions + Residual NAV) / Paid-in Capital = (900 + 200) / 500 = 1,100 / 500 = 2.2x, matching keyed option C. Workbook pp.153-154 define TVPI as cumulative distributions plus residual value divided by PIC, and equivalently as DPI + RVPI (here 1.8x + 0.4x = 2.2x). The Trap: 1.8x is DPI only (distributions-to-paid-in), missing the residual NAV. 1.4x is wrong arithmetic. 2.0x would imply 1,000/500, ignoring INR 100 crore. Note: Removed the side-by-side reporting commentary, the Fund II haircut framing, the realised-credibility pro-tip, and the Cross-Exam Context paragraph, since those go beyond the TVPI definition on pp.153-154.
